html:
A monastery in Constantinople, founded around 462 by the Roman consul Stoudios and dedicated to Saint John the Baptist. It became the most important monastery of the Byzantine Empire.

Its great age came under Theodore the Studite, abbot from about 799. He set a strict rule for common life, work and prayer, and built up a school and a workshop for copying books. He and his monks led the defence of holy images during the second period of Iconoclasm, and suffered exile and beatings for it.

The Studite rule was copied by the monks of Mount Athos, starting with the Great Lavra, and by the first great monasteries of Kievan Rus'. After the fall of the city in 1453 the church became a mosque. It now stands as a roofless ruin, the oldest surviving church in Istanbul.
sum: A monastery in Constantinople, founded around 462 by the Roman consul Stoudios and dedicated to Saint John the Baptist. It became the most important monastery of the Byzantine Empire.
